label: JavaScript
headline: JavaScript Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for JavaScript — variables, types, functions, arrays, objects, classes, promises, async/await, and the Fetch API.

items.name: let
items.definition: Block-scoped variable. Can be reassigned. Preferred for values that change.

items.name: const
items.definition: Block-scoped constant. Cannot be reassigned after declaration. Preferred by default.

items.name: var
items.definition: Function-scoped (or globally scoped). Hoisted to the top of its scope. Avoid in modern JS.

items.name: typeof
items.syntax:
typeof 42       // 'number'
typeof 'hi'     // 'string'
typeof true     // 'boolean'
typeof null     // 'object' (quirk)
typeof {}       // 'object'
typeof []       // 'object'
typeof fn       // 'function'
typeof undefined // 'undefined'
items.definition: Returns a string describing the type of the operand. Note: typeof null === 'object' is a historical quirk.

items.name: null vs undefined
items.syntax:
let a = null;      // intentionally empty
let b;             // undefined (not set)
items.definition: null is an intentional absence of value. undefined means a variable was declared but never assigned.

items.name: Template literals
items.definition: Backtick strings allow embedded expressions (${}) and multi-line content.

items.name: Arithmetic
items.definition: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, modulus (remainder), exponentiation (** is ES2016).

items.name: Strict equality
items.definition: === checks both value and type. Always prefer === over == to avoid implicit type coercion.

items.name: Loose equality
items.definition: == performs type coercion before comparing. Can produce surprising results — use === instead.

items.name: Logical AND / OR
items.syntax:
true && false  // false
false || true  // true
items.definition: Short-circuit operators. && returns the first falsy value; || returns the first truthy value.

items.name: Nullish coalescing (??)
items.definition: Returns the right side only if the left side is null or undefined. Unlike ||, 0 and '' are not treated as fallbacks.

items.name: Optional chaining (?.)
items.definition: Safely access nested properties. Returns undefined instead of throwing if any intermediate value is null/undefined.

items.name: Ternary
items.definition: Shorthand if/else expression. Returns one of two values based on a condition.

items.name: Spread (...)
items.definition: Expands an iterable or object into individual elements. Creates shallow copies.

items.name: Destructuring
items.syntax:
const { name, age } = person;
const [first, second] = arr;
items.definition: Unpack values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables.

items.name: length
items.definition: Returns the number of characters in the string.

items.name: toUpperCase / toLowerCase
items.definition: Return a new string converted to upper or lower case.

items.name: trim()
items.definition: Removes leading and trailing whitespace.

items.name: includes()
items.definition: Returns true if the string contains the given substring.

items.name: startsWith / endsWith
items.definition: Check whether a string begins or ends with a given substring.

items.name: slice()
items.definition: Extracts a portion from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive). Negative indices count from the end.

items.name: replace()
items.definition: Replaces the first match. Use /regex/g flag to replace all occurrences.

items.name: split()
items.definition: Splits a string into an array using the given separator.

items.name: padStart / padEnd
items.definition: Pads the start or end of a string to a target length.

items.name: repeat()
items.definition: Returns the string repeated n times.

items.name: push / pop
items.syntax:
arr.push('x');   // add to end
arr.pop();       // remove from end
items.definition: push() adds one or more elements to the end and returns the new length. pop() removes and returns the last element.

items.name: unshift / shift
items.syntax:
arr.unshift('x'); // add to start
arr.shift();      // remove from start
items.definition: unshift() adds to the start; shift() removes and returns the first element.

items.name: map()
items.definition: Returns a new array with each element transformed by the callback. Does not mutate the original.

items.name: filter()
items.definition: Returns a new array with only the elements for which the callback returns true.

items.name: reduce()
items.definition: Reduces an array to a single value by applying the callback with an accumulator and current element.

items.name: find() / findIndex()
items.syntax:
arr.find(n => n > 3)       // first match
arr.findIndex(n => n > 3)  // index of first match
items.definition: find() returns the first matching element; findIndex() returns its index. Both return undefined/-1 if not found.

items.name: includes()
items.definition: Returns true if the array contains the given value.

items.name: some() / every()
items.syntax:
arr.some(n => n > 3)   // at least one match
arr.every(n => n > 0)  // all match
items.definition: some() returns true if any element passes; every() returns true only if all elements pass.

items.name: flat() / flatMap()
items.definition: flat() flattens nested arrays by one level (or more with a depth argument). flatMap() combines map and flat.

items.name: slice()
items.definition: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of the array. Does not mutate the original.

items.name: splice()
items.definition: Mutates the array: removes elements at index 1, removes 2 elements, and inserts 'x' in their place.

items.name: sort()
items.syntax: arr.sort((a, b) => a - b);  // ascending numbers
items.definition: Sorts in-place. Without a comparator, sorts as strings. Pass a comparator for numeric or custom sorts.

items.name: forEach()
items.definition: Executes a function for each element. Returns undefined — use map() if you need a new array.

items.name: Array.from()
items.definition: Creates a new array from an iterable or array-like object. Accepts an optional mapping function.

items.name: Object literal
items.definition: Create an object with key/value pairs. Keys without spaces don't need quotes.

items.name: Shorthand property
items.syntax:
const name = 'Alice';
const person = { name };  // same as { name: name }
items.definition: If the variable name matches the key, you can omit the repetition.

items.name: Computed property
items.definition: Wrap the key in [] to use a dynamic expression as the property name.

items.name: Optional chaining
items.definition: Returns undefined instead of throwing when a property in the chain is null/undefined.

items.name: Object.keys()
items.definition: Returns an array of an object's own enumerable property names.

items.name: Object.values()
items.definition: Returns an array of an object's own enumerable property values.

items.name: Object.entries()
items.definition: Returns an array of [key, value] pairs for each own enumerable property.

items.name: Object.assign()
items.definition: Copies own enumerable properties from source objects into the target. Later sources overwrite earlier ones.

items.name: Spread merge
items.definition: Shallow merge objects. Properties in b overwrite matching properties in a.

items.name: delete operator
items.definition: Removes a property from an object.

items.name: Function declaration
items.definition: Hoisted to the top of its scope — can be called before it appears in the code.

items.name: Function expression
items.definition: Not hoisted. Assigned to a variable like any other value.

items.name: Arrow function
items.definition: Concise syntax. Implicit return when the body is a single expression (no braces). Does not bind its own this.

items.name: Default parameters
items.definition: Provide a default value used when the argument is undefined or omitted.

items.name: Rest parameters
items.definition: Collects all remaining arguments into an array.

items.name: Callback
items.definition: A function passed as an argument to another function, to be called later.

items.name: IIFE
items.definition: Immediately Invoked Function Expression — executes as soon as it is defined.

items.name: if / else if / else
items.definition: Standard conditional branching.

items.name: switch
items.definition: Matches a value against cases. Include break to prevent fall-through.

items.name: for loop
items.definition: Classic counted iteration with init, condition, and update.

items.name: for...of
items.definition: Iterate over iterable values (arrays, strings, Maps, Sets).

items.name: for...in
items.definition: Iterate over an object's enumerable property keys. Avoid for arrays.

items.name: while / do-while
items.definition: while checks before each iteration. do-while always runs the body at least once.

items.name: break / continue
items.syntax:
break;     // exit loop
continue;  // skip to next iteration
items.definition: break exits the loop entirely. continue skips the remaining body for the current iteration.

items.name: Class definition
items.definition: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. The constructor initializes each instance.

items.name: Inheritance
items.definition: extends inherits from a parent class. super() calls the parent constructor.

items.name: Static method
items.definition: Static methods belong to the class, not instances. Call directly on the class.

items.name: Getter / Setter
items.definition: get/set allow property-like access while executing logic.

items.name: Private fields (ES2022)
items.definition: Fields prefixed with # are private — inaccessible outside the class.

items.name: Named export
items.syntax:
export function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
export const PI = 3.14;
items.definition: Export one or more named bindings from a module file.

items.name: Default export
items.definition: Each module can have one default export. Import it with any name.

items.name: Named import
items.definition: Import specific named exports from a module.

items.name: Default import
items.definition: Import the default export. The name is chosen by the importer.

items.name: Rename import
items.definition: Use as to rename an import to avoid naming conflicts.

items.name: Import all
items.definition: Import all named exports as properties of a namespace object.

items.name: Create
items.definition: A Promise represents a value that may be available now, later, or never. Starts in pending state.

items.name: .then()
items.definition: Registers a callback for when the promise resolves. Returns a new promise for chaining.

items.name: .catch()
items.definition: Registers a callback for when the promise rejects.

items.name: .finally()
items.definition: Runs regardless of whether the promise resolved or rejected — good for cleanup.

items.name: Promise.all()
items.definition: Waits for all promises to resolve. Rejects immediately if any one rejects.

items.name: Promise.allSettled()
items.definition: Waits for all promises regardless of outcome. Each result has status (fulfilled/rejected) and value/reason.

items.name: Promise.race()
items.definition: Resolves or rejects as soon as the first promise settles.

items.name: async function
items.definition: Declares an async function. Always returns a Promise. Enables await inside the body.

items.name: await
items.definition: Pauses execution of the async function until the promise settles. Unwraps the resolved value.

items.name: try / catch errors
items.definition: Use try/catch to handle rejected promises when using await.

items.name: Parallel with await
items.definition: Kick off multiple promises simultaneously, then await all of them together.

items.name: GET request
items.syntax:
const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data');
const json = await res.json();
items.definition: fetch() returns a Promise. Call .json() on the response to parse the body as JSON.

items.name: POST request
items.definition: Pass an options object to send POST with a JSON body.

items.name: Check status
items.definition: fetch() does not reject on HTTP error codes (4xx, 5xx). Always check res.ok.

items.name: Response methods
items.syntax:
res.json()   // parse as JSON
res.text()   // parse as plain text
res.blob()   // parse as Blob (files, images)
items.definition: Each response method returns a Promise. You can only consume the body once.

items.name: try / catch / finally
items.definition: try wraps risky code, catch receives the Error object, finally always runs.

items.name: throw
items.definition: Throw any value as an error. Prefer throwing Error objects so stack traces are available.

items.name: Error types
items.definition: Built-in Error subtypes provide more specific information about what went wrong.
